title: Pela and Koru's Warm Hug
markdown:
It was a breezy afternoon down by the gentle, shimmering sea, a day when the wind liked to weave through everything, whispering and rustling the quiet air. Pela the penguin, with her smooth dark feathers, and Koru the seal pup, all soft fur and a nose that wiggled with happy curiosity, were waiting. They were waiting for their supper, a lovely meal of tasty fish. Oh, but the wind was so breezy it drifted right through them, making flippers and paws feel as chilly as little moonbeams.

Pela tucked her wings close. A soft shiver rippled through her sleek body. “Brrr,” she whispered, a low gentle rumble like faraway waves. “My feathers are usually so warm, like a downy quilt. They are very good at holding onto air. Today even the air between my feathers cannot keep the breeze away. It feels like a frost fairy tickling.”

Koru wriggled his whole body. His round nose twitched as he tried to shake off the cold. “Mine too!” he peeped. Soft brown fur ruffled like tiny waves on a pond. “I have lots of lovely fur, but the wind whispers icy tales right into my ears. My tummy feels like a cold pebble, even though it is full of warm blubber underneath.” He patted his plump belly, which usually felt like a cozy cushion. “My fur fluffs up, and the wind just blows it around. Quite a puzzle.”

They tried snuggling close, a little penguin and a little seal pup, nestled as tightly as could be. Pela felt Koru’s soft fur against her smooth feathers. Koru felt the close-knit hug of Pela’s coat. Still the wind found little places to slip through, like playful sprites dancing around them.

Pela looked at the grey sea. “When I swim, the water is cool, but it does not shiver me like this. It holds me. It does not blow through.”

Koru’s honey-colored eyes blinked. “Under my fur the blubber stays kind. When I dive, it keeps my own warmth in. Fur and blubber work together in the water. On this beach the wind unpicks them.”

Pela tilted her beak. “Your blubber is a cozy layer. My feathers hold tiny still rooms of air. Air is a helper: it stops warmth running away. If my air-holding feathers sit against your warmth-holding tummy, perhaps we can make a hug the wind cannot steal.”

And so Pela snuggled against Koru’s side, tucking her feathery wings right next to his soft, blubbery tummy. She nestled in, feeling warmth radiate from him. Koru leaned into her, feeling the gentle press of feathers. Oh, what a wonderful difference. The blubber kept Koru’s own body warmth steady, like a little furnace that asked for no wood. Pela’s feathers, filled with little pockets of still air, kept that warmth from being whisked away by the playful wind. It felt like being wrapped in the softest blanket, a lullaby of heat. The breeze still blew, making gentle sighing sounds. It could not reach them now. They were snug, waiting patiently for supper, waves a peaceful tick on the pebbles.

“This is lovely!” Koru sighed, nuzzling closer, nose tickling feathers. “We are warm. Truly warm.”

Pela nodded, a gentle smile on her beak. “That cozy layer has a name, my dear Koru. Insulation. It is like a hug that holds air, or slows heat, so warm stays warm and cool stays cool. My feathers hold air. Your fur is soft. Your blubber is a warm hug underneath. Together we made a better shield than either of us made alone.”

And wouldn’t you know it, soon their supper arrived: plump shimmering fish, smelling wonderfully fresh. As they ate, they looked at each other with a new quiet understanding. A breezy day could turn into a cozy adventure if you watched and thought. They wondered, with sleepy yawns escaping beaks and noses, what other clever secrets the world held — and how they might keep warm all through the night, nestled together, dreaming of the gentle ebb and flow of the tide.
